original_entry.title: Embedding theorem: local intersection forms are isometric to primitive Lefschetz forms
original_entry.strategy: Write M=B_xB_s, ell=ell(y), and use the exact Delta-flag sequence 0→Delta_y=Gamma_{≥y}B_y→B_y→Q→0. Under S(y), ch(Q)=underline H_y-H_y lies in vZ_{≥0}[v] on the standard basis, because it consists of the actual lower support layers of B_y. Also ch(M)=underline H_x underline H_s has nonnegative standard coefficients from its actual support flag. The Hom formula and graded freeness give an exact sequence 0→Hom^bullet(Q,M)→Hom^bullet(B_y,M)→Hom^bullet(Delta_y,M)→0: left exactness identifies the kernel, and the graded Hom formula gives additive graded ranks for all three free modules. Their graded Hilbert series are those ranks times the same polynomial-ring Hilbert series. Hence the image has exactly the Hilbert series of the target in every degree, proving surjectivity (a mere ungraded rank comparison would not suffice). In degrees ≤0 the first module vanishes; hence degree-zero restriction is an isomorphism Hom^0(B_y,M)→Hom^0(Delta_y,M), while no full graded isomorphism is asserted. Hom(Delta_y,M) identifies with Gamma_yM shifted by ell, and the same degree bound makes Gamma_yM supported in degrees ≥ell. The support-layer inclusion is a right-module summand by the finite support-filtration/localization supplier; thus reduction injects its degree-ell part into Mbar^ell (if a vector belongs to Gamma_yM∩M R_+, project to that summand to put it in Gamma_yM R_+, whose degree-ell part is zero). A generator c of Delta_y maps to a nonzero generator of B_ybar^ell; evaluation at c therefore injects degree-zero Hom into Mbar^ell. Since HR(y) gives hL(y), rho^ell c_bot is a nonzero scalar multiple of c after reduction. If f(c_bot) vanished then f(rho^ell c_bot) would vanish, contradicting that injection. This proves injectivity of bottom evaluation. The reduced B_y is supported in [-ell,ell], so rho^{ell+1} annihilates c_bot after reduction, and bimodule linearity puts the image in P^{-ell}. For the isometry, g* f is the local scalar, so N(f,g)=<g* f(c_bot),rho^ell c_bot>_{B_y}=<f(c_bot),rho^ell g(c_bot)>_M, with N>0 by the normalized HR(y) form. Definite primitive forms restrict to definite forms on these images; the detection theorem then gives S(xs).

original_entry.title: Hard Lefschetz for the deformed operator on B_x B_s, in the three cases
original_entry.statement:
The hard Lefschetz theorem for $L_\zeta$ on $M=B_x^RB_s^R$ holds in the following three cases.

(1) $\zeta>0$ and $xs<x$: under $\mathrm S(x)$, $\mathrm{hL}(x)$ implies $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_\zeta$. The $\mathrm{hL}(x)$-only descent implication, with the same matrix and without an assumed $\mathrm S(x)$, is retained as an after-induction consequence in the character theorem, where $\mathrm S(x)$ has already been proved.

(2) $\zeta>0$ and $xs>x$: if $\mathrm S(\le x)$, $\mathrm{HR}(z,t)$ for all $z<x$ and simple $t$ with $zt>z$, $\mathrm{HRbar}(<x,s)_\zeta$ and $\mathrm{HR}(x)$ hold, then $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds.

(3) $\zeta=0$ and $xs>x$: if $\mathrm S(\le x)$, $\mathrm{HR}(z,t)$ for all $z<x$ and simple $t$ with $zt>z$, $\mathrm{HR}(x)$ and $\mathrm{hL}(z)$ for all $z<xs$ hold, then $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)$ holds.

In the remaining case $\zeta=0$ and $xs<x$, centered hard Lefschetz fails: in the decomposition $B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$ the operator $L_0$ is diagonal, the bottom vector of the first summand lies in degree $-\ell(x)-1$ and its $(\ell(x)+1)$-st $\rho$-power is zero, while the opposite total degree is nonzero by self-duality; the two copies have Lefschetz strings centered at $-1$ and $+1$ rather than at zero.
original_entry.strategy: Case (1): apply the local simple-invariants descent lemma under S(x). It gives B_x=N⊗_{R^s}R and the explicit reduced matrix [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]] on B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1). The local supplier proves hL by an explicit binomial power calculation on each primitive rho string tensored with the centered two-dimensional string; the middle matrices have determinant 1 and the extreme map is multiplication by the nonzero integer m+1. At zeta=0 the bottom class b∈B_xbar^{-ell(x)} has degree -ell(x)-1 in B_x(1)bar and rho^{ell(x)+1}b=0, giving failure of centered hL. Case (2): put x=s_1...s_m, gamma_i=(s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^vee)>0 and gamma_{m+1}=(x^{-1}rho)(alpha_s^vee)+zeta rho(alpha_s^vee)>0. The deleted-word factorization and chosen minimal-complex embedding give <b,L_zeta b'>=<phi b,phi b'>_gamma for the first differential phi:F_xF_s^0=B_xB_s→(^1F_x)B_s⊕B_x(1). After reduction it commutes with L_zeta on the first target and rho on B_x(1); the extra right zeta rho term on the second target vanishes. Reduced cohomology makes phi injective in degrees ≤ell(x). With W=(^1F_x)(-1)B_s⊕B_x, the map lands in W(1). The unshifted (^1F_x)(-1) has the induced HR signs by the Rouquier supplier, and its lower indecomposable summands satisfy HR(y,s)_zeta; the tensoring lemma gives HR on its B_s product. HR(x) supplies the other orthogonal target component. Positive rescalings preserve signs, so the weak-Lefschetz substitute gives injectivity of every L_zeta^k, and self-duality gives equal source/target dimensions. Case (3): take the same positive gamma scalars with zeta=0 and split (^1F_x)(-1)=B_up⊕B_down orthogonally, with summands B_y satisfying respectively ys>y and ys<y. The descent supplier applies to lower y since S(y) is known. Cancel the contractible tau_{≤-2}(B_down B_s(1)) against the next differential by the perverse lower-bound supplier; the remaining first differential is d=(d_1,d_2,d_3):B_xB_s→B_x(1)⊕B_up B_s(1)⊕B_down and remains injective in degrees ≤ell(x). All components commute with left rho. For a nonzero b in degree -k, if d_3(b)≠0, the assumed hL on every lower B_y gives rho^k d_3(b)≠0 and hence rho^k b≠0. Otherwise put V=ker d_3 and W=B_x⊕B_up B_s. The map (d_1,d_2):V→W(1) is injective in negative degrees and form-compatible: the removed shifted-descent piece has identically zero Lefschetz forms by the degenerate-shift lemma, so <phi b,phi b'>=<b,rho b'> on V. HR on W follows from HR(x), HR(y,s) for the ascent summands and the tensoring lemma. The weak-Lefschetz substitute gives rho^k injective on V^{-k}. These two cases give hL on the whole source by dimension symmetry. No step assumes HR for the unseparated zero-parameter descent target, and no step invokes the unconditional singular-category descent theorem.
